findings.current: روکی گئی / خرابی کے ساتھ رک گئی
findings.problem: Both are unanchored turn markers, so the reader supplies the head noun, and this pair supplies a FEMININE one while the same file's sibling turn marker supplies an impersonal masculine: ui.chat.canonical.transcript.stopped_before_finishing = 'مکمل ہونے سے پہلے روک دیا گیا'. The split is visible inside one transcript family. The feminine itself is defensible and consistent with the two shipped 'Interrupted' markers (ui.chat.canonical.transcript.interrupted and ui.chat.canonical.tool_row.outcome.interrupted, both 'روکی گئی'), which is why no value change is demanded here: this is recorded so the family converges on ONE agreement rather than drifting further.
findings.suggested: Keep both values as they are; converge the sibling instead (transcript.stopped_before_finishing -> 'مکمل ہونے سے پہلے روکی گئی'), so every closed-turn marker agrees feminine as the two 'Interrupted' markers already do. If the file owner prefers impersonal masculine, then all four strings must move together, e.g. 'روکا گیا' / 'خرابی کے ساتھ رکا گیا'.

findings.problem: The heading reads as a bare prepositional phrase where the catalogue's own house pattern for 'without X' carries the postposition: ui.chat.tags.shown_untagged = 'بغیر ٹیگ کے گروہ میں'. 'بغیر گروہ' is understandable and does read as a category rather than an agent name (the sidecar's requirement), and the noun choice is right: 'گروہ' is the settled term for a chat grouping in this catalogue (ui.chat.sidebar_view.group_by = 'گروہ بندی', ui.chat.sidebar.badge 'اس گروہ میں', ui.chat.tags.show_under 'اس گروہ میں رکھیں', ui.notifications.group 'گروہ بندی'), while 'گروپ' is the teamBridge/canvas sense of a literal group conversation. Graded NIT, not MINOR: nothing is misread.

findings.current: سب {count, number, ::group-off} پڑھا ہوا نشان زد کریں
findings.problem: Fit only. Rendered with a two-digit count this is 26 cells against 16 for 'Mark all 12 read' (1.6x); the sidecar calls the slot a narrow section header beside Active chats, and the span carries `truncate` with a shed to sr-only below a 253px container (src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/chat-sidebar.tsx:438,2332). An ellipsis would cut the final imperative 'کریں' - the verb - though the accessible name survives. Wording, order, ICU skeleton and idiom are correct, and the shape matches the shipped precedent ui.notifications.action.mark_all_read = 'سب پڑھا ہوا نشان زد کریں' with the count inserted (the count must stay: UX U1). Not measured in a renderer.
findings.suggested: No text change proposed. Flag for the rendered narrow-width check; if it does ellipsise, the shortest correct alternative is 'سب {count} پڑھا نشان زد کریں' (drops the 'ہوا' of 'پڑھا ہوا', still the shipped read-state word) at 22 cells.

observations_not_counted.detail: OUTSIDE my seven keys, pre-existing, not counted: markAllReadCopy builds `scope` (bound to the control's `title`, chat-sidebar.tsx:2287) and `nameSuffix` (its accessible name tail) from hardcoded English template strings - 'Mark ${count} unread ${chat} as read, including ${elsewhere} in Previous chats.' and '${tokenless} unread marks with no completion token cannot be cleared.' - so in ur the keyed visible label is Urdu while the tooltip and part of the accessible name stay English. Reported for the manager; it does not bear on this pass's verdict.

RTL/bidi sanity, verified by reading the runtime seam and not by rendering: `{name}` in ui.chat.canonical.link_toolkit.actions_for is a plain argument, so isolateArguments wraps the Latin-led value in FSI...PDI for an RTL-answered message, and the leading position is correct because the container is dir=rtl (the Latin isolate paints at the right edge, then 'کے لیے', then 'اقدامات'). The `{count}` digits in mark_all_read.label need no isolate by that module's own rule (bare digits are neutral-safe after RTL text; Urdu letters are AL, so W2/N1 keep the digits in place). No manual bidi control (U+200E/F, U+061C, U+202A-E, U+2066-9) appears in any of the seven values, as the style guide requires.

The colon/dash pair distinction is preserved exactly as the sidecars ask (':' when the runtime reason carries no colon, ' — ' when it does), the {detail} placeholder sits in the same position and is inserted verbatim, and both separators are neutral between an RTL phrase and an LTR {detail}, so N1/N2 resolve them to the paragraph direction (RTL) and they paint after the Urdu phrase in reading order. Reasoning from the bidi algorithm, not measured with fribidi or a renderer.
